exposure: subcutaneous injection of autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) during caesarean wound closure
cohort: The study included 44 women undergoing caesarean section, divided into two groups.
finding: Prophylactic administration of autologous PRP during caesarean wound closure significantly improved wound quality and reduced the development of Surgical Site Infections (SSI) in the post-operative period.
mod_finding: Prophylactic autologous PRP administration during caesarean wound closure significantly improved wound quality and reduced SSI, demonstrating a benefit specifically for caesarean mode of birth.
